I've been working this land for 35 years. I know this soil, I know Quzhou's weather, and I know what works. My 9 mu runs the same rotation every year — wheat goes in after National Day in October, I harvest it in June, then maize goes straight in and I pull that by late September. Same ground, two crops, one year. My wife and I can manage it ourselves.

For wheat, I don't mess around with unfamiliar seeds. I'll use the improved variety the village seed shop carries — not the most expensive, but I've used it before and it yields reliably. I put down compound fertilizer at planting as base, then spread urea at jointing. Three irrigations: the winter water before freeze, jointing, and heading. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide early on, one fungicide spray around heading when powdery mildew shows up. I do rotary tillage after I harvest the maize stubble to work it in.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed — everyone here does now, the yield difference is too big to ignore. I plant it right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste. I put base fertilizer down at planting and topdress at tasseling. Summer rains help but I pump from the well at least twice — once around big bell stage, once if August turns dry. Two pesticide applications, one for fall armyworm if it shows up, one general spray.

I don't experiment much. At my age, with just two of us, I need predictable crops, not surprises.
